mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which may lead to negative equity returns as economic growth falters.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 posts positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows after UNRATE increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which is positive for equity markets.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts and retail sales increase, it signals strong demand, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If both proxies increase but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests a strong supply chain and economic growth, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates coupled with low unemployment may signal tight monetary conditions, negatively impacting equity markets.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 posts positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows under these conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth indicates weakening demand, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth in a late-cycle expansion may indicate peak employment, leading to negative equity returns as growth falters.
failure_condition: If payroll growth is strong but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.
